A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DiffVSR. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite the changed title and substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark results, component and training-strategy ablations, qualitative comparisons, and a 20-participant user study.

after.justification: v3 retains original experiments and reports additional degradation tests, component ablations, and runtime comparisons.

M1.justification: The backbone, three-stage progressive learning strategy, MSTA, temporal-enhanced VAE and its losses, and ILT with noise rescheduling are retained. Promoting progressive learning to the central contribution does not change the algorithm; newly specified implementation details do not establish procedural changes.

E1.justification: v3 removes REDS4 and SPMCS, two of v1's four synthetic evaluation collections, and adds a complex-degradation UDM10 scenario. This substantially refocuses synthetic coverage. The YouHQ40 conditions, real-world collections including appendix VideoLQ, and training dataset sources remain.

E2.justification: VEnhancer is removed from the main quantitative comparison, although retained in the VideoLQ table and quality-consistency plot. v3 adds UAV-style flow alignment as an alternative to ILT in Table 4 and noise alternatives in Figure 7. Most benchmark comparators are unchanged.

E3.justification: The shared training setup remains unchanged. v3 drops BC/TF benchmark reporting and emphasizes synthetic warping-error evaluation; its component ablation replaces SSIM/TF with LPIPS/MUSIQ. It also introduces runtime measurement on video 000 and additional ablation controls. TF remains in the relocated VAE comparison.

E4.justification: v3 adds removal of the combined architectural enhancements, an isolated MSTA ablation, ILT-versus-flow runtime/quality analysis, training-stage visual analysis, and noise-transition comparisons. These materially expand component validation. The direct/two-stage/three-stage training comparison was already in v1's appendix and is relocated, not newly introduced.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests. The user-study participant count, test-set count, and preference reporting remain unchanged.

E6.justification: v3 adds complex-UDM10 results, including DiffVSR CLIP-IQA 0.726 and MUSIQ 66.431, and new architectural, noise, and runtime findings. REDS4/SPMCS scores and the separate temporal-comparison results are removed. All 140 matched entries in the main benchmark tables are unchanged, as are the retained training-strategy, VAE, VideoLQ, and user-preference results.

T1.justification: The diffusion objective, temporal-attention equations, and ILT interpolation formula are retained with renumbering. Neither version supplies formal propositions or proofs; the expanded learning-burden argument is conceptual interpretation rather than new mathematical theory.

C1.justification: v1 presents four innovations addressing restoration quality and temporal consistency. v3 makes progressive learning the core contribution and advances the broader claim that learning burden, rather than architectural sophistication, is the primary bottleneck for severe degradations. Its abstract also narrows the temporal-performance claim from superiority to competitive consistency.

C2.justification: v3 interprets the experiments as establishing learning strategy's dominance over architecture, attributes Stage 2 shortcomings to WebVid overfitting, and explicitly discusses ILT's perceptual-quality and runtime trade-offs. These extend v1's optimization rationale substantially. The original limitations concerning inference speed, small subjects, complex scenes, and limited training scale remain.

D1.justification: v3 specifies an approximately 400K-pair WebVid2M training subset and 2× MSTA downsampling, but removes the explicit InternLM-XComposer2 prompt-generation description. v1 described WebVid's overall size without specifying this subset, so an actual training-data reduction is not established. Hardware, optimizer, batch size, cropping, and project access information remain.

R1.justification: The broad image/video restoration survey is substantially condensed, removing discussion and citations for several GAN and transformer approaches, while FreeNoise is added. More fundamentally, v3 positions DiffVSR against architecture-focused research and attributes competing methods' failures primarily to their learning burden.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, related work, method narrative, experimental discussion, and conclusion are extensively rewritten around progressive learning. PLS moves ahead of the architectural components, those components are consolidated, and ablations precede benchmark comparisons. This is substantial narrative restructuring.

P2.justification: v3 merges the main qualitative comparisons, adds training-stage imagery and noise-profile panels, restructures benchmark and ablation tables, and introduces runtime and MSTA tables. The training-strategy display moves into the main text, the VAE table moves to the appendix, and appendix prose changes to a single-column layout. Existing appendix galleries are retained.

improvement.justification: The added architectural controls, ILT runtime comparison, and harder UDM10 evaluation strengthen empirical scrutiny. However, v3 removes benchmark and temporal-metric evidence while advancing a broader causal claim about learning strategy that the reported comparisons do not fully establish. Its retained no-computational-overhead assertion also conflicts with Table 4's runtime increase from 424.81 to 727.85 seconds with ILT. These gains in validation and losses in breadth and claim calibration leave the net quality change uncertain.
